# Gateway and safety (area `gateway`)

Boundaries code enforces: confirmations, protection lists, terminal typing, redaction, secrets and the sealed fill path, owner identity.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **GATE-1** (agent): FERB's launchd definitions (the user LaunchAgent plists and FERB.app's BUNDLE_SERVICE) are FERB_SERVICE, never lifted; the shell profile denies writing them. A daemon not run from FERB.app (from ~/.ferb/venv or a checkout) also protects the installed FERB.app (/Applications, then ~/Applications, with FERB's bundle id) like the bundled one: never written or removed by FERB's tools or shell, its service definition counted as FERB's. Read at daemon start.
- **GATE-2** (agent): OwnerSecrets.delete deletes the Keychain item through the signed helper that made it (its delete operation: SecItemDelete by service and account), never reading it first; an item not found counts as deleted, and an item another entry still names stays. It is journaled secret.deleted with place and name only. secrets.saved shows place, name and kind, never a value, Keychain account or username.
- **GATE-200** (owner): For the escape hatch and the file tools, one read question per protected folder per task covers every read of that folder in the task. Writes and admin still ask per command.
- **GATE-201** (agent): The foreground Need is keyed by confirm.app_key: the running app's bundle id (casefolded) when the name, `pid:N` or bundle id names exactly one running app, else the argument without case or invisible marks. The question shows the app as the worker wrote it. One Yes covers every spelling and retry in the task.
- **GATE-202** (owner): Tools report structural facts (a form submit and its action host, card/password field types, the checkout amount on the page, the recipient a mail/message tool uses); facts raise the question. The worker's `effect` declaration can only add a question, never remove one.
- **GATE-203** (owner): File tools are bound by the never-read and never-write protection lists, like the shell. A task that needs a listed place asks the owner: reads once per protected folder per task (GATE-200), writes per action.
- **GATE-204** (owner): Asked once when the final amount is known, with amount and merchant read from the page by code (never the worker's number; if unreadable, the question says so). The Yes covers that payment in this task's tab and what it opens until it completes or 10 minutes pass; another tab or task asks again. A bank page whose amount or merchant differs asks again showing both; an OTP question repeats them. With no bank page, it asks at the final pay click; a changed amount asks again. Known sites never skip it.
- **GATE-205** (owner): Recipients and sites the owner approved stay known for good. Sites mentioned in a request are known for normal use in that and later tasks; only sending private data there after outside content was read still asks once.
- **GATE-206** (owner): Card fields (autocomplete cc-number / cc-csc / cc-exp) are secret fields like password and OTP fields: values never captured in snapshots, boxes masked in screenshots; card details are filled only through the sealed path (stored once in the Keychain) or the site's / browser's saved card. The redactor masks CVV beside its label and expiry beside a card. Storing a card works like other owner secrets: asked, hidden input, models see only a handle.
- **GATE-207** (owner): One "don't ask for 30 minutes" answer covers routine questions only: the foreground question, protected-folder read lifts, a browser's own pages, new recipients and profile pairing. It never covers payments, account security, permanent deletion, terminal typing, certificate checks turned off or the sink question. The window is one value for the gateway, spanning tasks until it ends; Yeses inside it record destinations like normal Yeses.
- **GATE-210** (owner): The redaction rebuild keeps the owner-decided details: the address-code exemption, CODE_REACH 8 (a code word reaches a code across at most 8 words), and dictionary-word secrets (a sealed dictionary word is matched as a whole word).
- **GATE-211** (agent): All reviewed OTP rules are kept (email layouts, markup, backup-code lists).
- **GATE-212** (agent): Card numbers are checked (Luhn) over every window of digit groups, so `qty 2 <card>` is caught. Expiry is masked only in MM/YY form after an expiry label or right after a card; CVV only beside its label (or after a card and expiry).
- **GATE-213** (agent): The daemon preloads saved-secret values (and API keys only for runtimes in use) into the known-value registry at start, so they are masked before their first fill. Test daemons never preload.
- **GATE-214** (agent): A submitted form with a card field (cc-number/cc-csc/cc-exp) asks as a payment. A current-password field together with a new_password field asks as account security; a sign-up's new-password field alone asks nothing. A tool's `deletes` outside the Trash ask as permanent delete of each path (counted first if a folder). Each fact kind is decided with its own target and provenance; the union with the declaration's needs is asked.
- **GATE-215** (agent): Every submitted form goes to the sink rule only: asked when a value typed or chosen into that tab carries the owner's private data by provenance, after outside content was read, to the form's action host (else the page's) that the owner neither named in this request nor approved. A submit with no private value never asks (GET or POST) and never raises the new-recipient question. The test-mode allowlist covers fact payments, not fact form submits.
- **GATE-216** (agent): A browser payment's Yes is keyed to its tab chain (the first task tab that opened it). A Mac app's payment is scoped to its app window (bundle + window id) for 10 minutes; a payment with neither asks every run, showing an unread amount unless the capability describes it. The worker's declared amount is never shown or keyed. Bank page = the tab moved to another host, or the input is in a frame of another host (a payment gateway's card frame too: only a differing amount/merchant asks there).
- **GATE-217** (agent): Complete (next payment asks): a call ran on another host and the chain came back to the checkout's host; a second card form is submitted there; or a one-click paying submit with no card form or bank page before it. Amounts compare by currency and number (a side with no currency compares the number); merchants case- and space-insensitively; an amount read where the approved one was unread asks again. Approvals live in memory (a restart asks again); a No is keyed by chain + amount + merchant and stays final.
- **GATE-218** (agent): KnownDestinations.approved (answered or confirmed) is the sink rule's test; known (any how) stays the new-recipient and outside-value test. A named destination is upgraded when the owner later approves it, never downgraded. Stored keys and values: the text when the redactor leaves it alone, sha256:<digest> when it would change it without a specific hit, never stored or matched when Redactor.hit finds a saved secret or credential format.
- **GATE-219** (agent): Owner secrets saved from a card field keep their kind and fill only a field of the same kind; a card field takes only an entry of its kind or a one-time hidden input. The gateway refuses typed text into a card field and a Luhn-valid card number typed anywhere.
- **GATE-220** (agent): An exception from a tool counts as failed (retry not blocked, the owner's Yes released) when it is Refused (any subclass), a pydantic ValidationError, or carries attempted = False; anything else is unknown for the repeat check (P19). The call's span is finished whatever escapes.
- **GATE-221** (agent): Each confirm.Need carries `reaches` (the target it was decided for: the call's, a fact's, a counted folder) and StandingPermissions.covers compares the scope's site and recipients with that target; tool, identity, account and content stay the call's.
- **GATE-222** (agent): mac.applescript addressed to a web browser (the one browser list) takes the same foreground question as Mac input there (same key: one Yes covers the browser for the task whichever Mac tool acts); a quoted browser page address in the script (chrome://extensions…) asks every time like input on that page. Not refused.
- **GATE-223** (agent): MacAppleScript.file_paths reports each quoted POSIX path and HFS path on a mounted volume as a change, so the one gateway file check applies: FERB's own state, FERB.app and its service definitions refused whatever the owner said, a listed place asks per call.
- **GATE-224** (agent): protection.BROWSER_STORES is browsers.data_folders(): each Chromium browser's user-data folder and the other browsers' data (Safari and its container, Firefox, makers' shared folders). An older config.toml gets each default it was never offered once (journal config.defaults_added), so the owner's own entries and removals stay.
- **GATE-225** (owner): Every question card shows one question. A confirmation's is built by code from its needs with the facts that decide it (the app and how long the Yes lasts, the exact command, amount and merchant, path and count, recipients and text, the profile, a value and its source), plus the task's reason as one small line; the step and raw call stay only in the record. A retry asks in plain words. A task's question carries a structural "from the task" tag instead of a text prefix.
- **GATE-501** (owner): A secret pasted into the chat is masked before any model sees it (every format in the named table plus saved secret values) and the message still runs. FERB adds one reminder under it naming each kind once: it hid it from the AI and didn't save it, and keys and passwords are best not pasted into chats. A saved secret is named as one of the owner's saved secrets. No advice to revoke: the value never left the Mac.
- **GATE-502** (agent): The notice comes from the redactor's finding, never from a model, so it always appears; it names kinds, never the value. The owner's bubble shows the masked text (the ack's message), also after a restart; the journal records chat.secret_hidden with kinds only; the planner gets the hidden kinds as one fact, so a reply never asks the owner to paste it again. The kinds are formats, not intent (AGENTS.md rule 4): nothing is refused.
- **GATE-503** (owner): FERB may write the clipboard and may approve another agent's prompts (owner 2026-10-07: "no, let it do this").
- **GATE-504** (owner): The front window (topmost non-FERB window) is screenshotted, redacted, with every message for the planner and reused by the worker; browser windows, task tabs and recording frames go redacted; an image is withheld only when masking fails; excluded sites are captured as excluded, excluded apps are not looked at or named; never the whole desktop.
- **GATE-505** (agent): A protection-list entry that is another app's container or inside one (~/Library/Containers/<id>, ~/Library/Group Containers/<id>, as typed or under those folders resolved) is never stat'ed, resolved or opened: its resolved form is the containers folder resolved plus the rest as written, it counts as a folder for the shell profile, and a folder above it inside a container is denied as present. The containers folders themselves may be looked at. Paths a tool call names are still checked as the kernel reaches them.
- **GATE-506** (agent): The browser URL sink (sink:private_url) does not count a value whose every private occurrence is inside a URL of the destination's host (as before) or in a record read from the destination's own site: a record whose outside labels are only web pages of hosts the destination covers (same host, www aside, or a host under it; never a sibling) plus at most the private label. A value also found anywhere else in private text (a file, another site's page, FERB's context, a mixed record) still counts. Read order (N1), followed links and decoded words (N2) are unchanged.
- **GATE-507** (agent): sink:private_url says which value of the owner's the address would send (the matched token, and the address piece it rides in when that differs, e.g. a decoded or embedded value) and where this task first read it (a file by path, a tool result by tool and site, or the context FERB gave the model), from span facts only, never the record's content beyond the value.
- **GATE-508** (agent): Argument provenance (S3) lists `private` for a value found in a tool result of the tree whose labels are only the private label (and the owner's): a file, an app, nothing outside. S4(b) (sink:outside_value) asks only when a value came only from outside content: not when it is in the owner's words, answers or such a result. A mixed record (a signed-in page holding outside content) is not the owner's own for this. The question says FERB found it only in outside content, not "not from you". New-recipient, standing scopes and the sink rule are unchanged.
- **GATE-509** (agent): The browser and Mac typing tools record a typed email address or phone number as the call's recipient (provenance.typed_destination), never a URL: a URL addresses no one. Typed into a field it is data; opening it is navigation, which the browser URL sink and the foreground and browser-page questions cover. Typed emails and phone numbers keep the S4(b) provenance question at typing time, because a browser send (a JS Send button) has no structural fact (act_kind is physical only; T-201) and the typing is the only structural point where an injected recipient is seen.
- **GATE-510** (owner): A task's safety check (confirmation, retry, conversation scope) shows its options and a box "Or tell the task something else" (chat.correct). Words there never count as Yes or No: the action doesn't run, they reach that check's task as the owner's correction by structure and the check is set aside (ORCH-538); the card goes at once. Redacted as a chat message is. Exact option words count as that option. Refused for closed questions and checks with no task. chat.answer words on FERB's checks: "Pick Yes or No."
- **GATE-511** (agent): confirm.pair_need takes the profile's signed-in account (GatewayDeps.profile_account, read fresh) into its values, and the question and its short form say it in brackets after the profile's name. The owner-named check (provenance) still compares only the profile's name, so "pair my Work profile" skips the question as before, and the need's key stays (browser, folder).
- **GATE-512** (agent): Approval.option_for counts an option's number only for a task's own question. FERB's own checks (questions.OWN_CHECKS, the same five as steering.FERB_CHECKS: confirmation, P19 retry, conversation scope, forget, downloads cap) and FERB's check-ins (options_only) take only an option's own words, in chat.answer, in the box (chat.correct) and in chat; a typed "1" there is words: refused on the card ("Pick Yes or No."), a correction in the box, never a Yes. Buttons (chat.approve with a choice) are unchanged.
- **GATE-513** (owner): Refines GATE-225's card. Each of FERB's own questions (confirmations, passwords, login codes, the Mac password) is a plain question in the normal font, a line saying why FERB asks, and the exact thing approved (command, address, value, path, amount) in a code box; no tool names. A password question still starts with its place. A kind without new words keeps today's sentence; a card that can't be built asks with today's line. The full question stays in the record.
- **GATE-514** (agent): For GATE-513, after the owner asked a fresh agent to review the wording: a card whose Yes makes a person or site known for good (SQ6, GATE-205) says so; sharing data names the value sent; a new site says the task read your own data; the code box holds only the value (its source goes in the why); terminal cards name the app once and say a Yes covers one input; payments say they take money, and a different bank amount says it differs.
- **GATE-515** (agent): History lines (task answers, FERB's replies and questions written from outside content, notices) show origin.shown: the stored labels, except that a record with more than one outside label shows each outside kind once (external:web), never the hosts and senders it inherited; one outside label keeps its detail. A tool result's footer names what the tool itself read with its detail, and labels passed through from FERB's records (chat.history, memory.read, task.evidence) that way. Outside entries stay marked and quoted as data. Display only: stored labels and every check are unchanged.
